title: Affine etale cover by a disjoint union of affines
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $E$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Write $|E|$ for the set of field-valued point classes of $E$: maps $\operatorname{Spec}K\to E$ with $K$ a field [def-weil-field], two such maps being identified when they agree after restriction to a common field extension; a morphism $t:h_T\to E$ from a scheme $T$ induces $|t|:|T|\to|E|$, sending a point $x$ to the class of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to T\to E$. There exist a scheme $W$ that is a disjoint union of affine schemes and a representable surjective etale morphism $w:h_W\to E$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] such that $|w|:|W|\to|E|$ is surjective. The affine components may be chosen so that each maps into an affine open subscheme of $S$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Give $|E|$ the quotient topology of $|w|$; it does not depend on the choice of the representable surjective etale map $w$ from a scheme. With this topology, for every scheme $T$ and every morphism $t:h_T\to E$ the map $|t|:|T|\to|E|$ is continuous, and if $t$ is representable etale, then $|t|$ is open; in particular its image is open in $|E|$.
